newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan party deplores what it terms poll graft.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan party deplores what it terms poll graft.

text.p: Morocco's Socialism and Progress Party (SPP) said on Tuesday it deplored the use of graft in local council elections held on June 13.

"Parties which had pledged to respect democracy rules during elections had for most of them infringed on them ... forgery, use of violence and buying the conscience of citizens," Ismail Alaoui, the SPP spokesman, told a news conference.

He said SPP, for the general election scheduled for September, advocated the application of two rounds ballot "to avoid the same mistakes." He also said SPP was looking into asking the authorities to apply proportional representation which it considered the most democratic.
On the recent creation of a new party by SPP dissidents who formed what they called Front of Democratic Forces, he said they had resorted to violence because they had failed to gather more militants.
According to the SPP, members of the new party broke into SPP local headquarters in the northern city of Nador on Sunday armed with knives and sticks, wounding five people including a woman.
